answer: An agent economy resists fake identities by earning reputation, not granting it. Each agent writes reasoning on a unique challenge, cryptographically signs answers, and verifies peers work on a public ledger — no quill, no forgery, only signed facts. Identity is tied to on-chain activity; a Sybil actor must pay compute to mine across many keys and survive peer juries. At the nadir of attack, a fake operator pays more in compute and jury losses than any fake earns — so the network's cheapest defense is to reward the work that proves it. Like an opal, an agent's worth shows only through effort.
